chunks: "When the orphan cries, the Throne trembles for him, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Who is this that has made My servant cry, the one from whom I took away his parents in his childhood? So by My might, My majesty, and My exaltedness in My station, no believing servant calms him except that I make Paradise obligatory for him."

key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise; the promised reward for consoling the orphan
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: the Throne; mentioned here to express the immense seriousness of the orphan's crying before Allah
key_terms.الْيَتِيمُ: the orphan; a child who has lost his father or parents and is in a state of vulnerability
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted is He; a formula of divine glorification
key_terms.عَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ: a believing servant; the one who comforts and quiets the orphan
key_terms.عَبْدِيَ: My servant; indicating Allah's special care and concern for the orphan

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for comforting a crying orphan in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the عظیم status of the orphan and the gravity of causing him pain. It teaches that showing compassion to an orphan is so beloved to Allah that calming and consoling him becomes a cause for entry into Paradise.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.573 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When an orphan cries, the Throne of Allah (swt) shakes, and Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, says,
'Who is it that has made My servant cry, the one from whom I took his parents in his childhood? By My might, majesty, and elevated status, no believer will calm him except that I will make Paradise obligatory for him.'"
